title: trace-merge-adaptor-and-annotator
content:
Purpose and high level
---------------------
This is a working doc for the Trace Merge Adaptor: a small, opinionated post-processing toolkit that ingests heterogeneous profiler outputs (perf script stacks, eBPF samples, OpenTelemetry spans, GPU CUPTI timelines, and our existing token-level KV-cache logs) and produces canonical outputs for:
  - folded stacks for FlameGraph generation
  - canonical JSONL traces for trace-explorer (time-aligned spans + annotations)
  - lightweight aggregated CSVs for CI regression diffs

Why we need it
--------------
We have multiple collectors (eBPF user-space samples, runtime-internal span emitters, GPU traces) that are useful in different investigations. But they have different timestamp bases, PID/TID formats, sampling granularities, and often duplicate the same logical event (e.g., a runtime 'emit' span and an eBPF sample capturing the same stack). The adaptor does:
  1) normalize time to a single wall-clock epoch (with best-effort cross-clock alignment using perf_clock sync markers)
  2) deduplicate overlapping spans/samples into a single canonical event with provenance tags
  3) attach runtime metadata (model name, seq len, request id, shard id) from KV-cache logs when available
  4) output multiple downstream formats so CI, flamegraph, and trace explorer can reuse a single artifact

Design goals / constraints
------------------------
- lightweight, CLI-first (python3.10 + small deps), suitable for CI jobs that run in <2 minutes on synthetic traces.
- deterministic merging (idempotent runs on same inputs) so CI diffs are stable.
- preserve provenance: we never drop raw ids — every canonical event includes a list of source contributors.
- backwards compatible JSONL schema so the trace explorer ingest doesn't break older dashboards.
- privacy: scrub PII and customer identifiers by default unless --keep-ids is passed and user is in ops group.

Quickstart (local)
------------------
# example: merge perf + otel + kvcache logs and output folded stacks for flamegraph
$ trace-adapt 
  --inputs perf.out.txt,otel.jsonl,kvcache.csv 
  --sync-markers perf_clock_sync.json 
  --out-folded merged.flamefold 
  --out-trace merged.canonical.jsonl

Notes: perf.out.txt is the output of `perf script` after generating raw.data; otel.jsonl is the tracer exported with our JSON exporter; kvcache.csv is a simplified CSV we emit in synthetic workloads.

CI integration (perf-ci)
-----------------------
- Add a step in perf CI that runs `trace-adapt --inputs $ARTIFACTS --out-csv ci_aggregate.csv` and then the existing perf-diff step compares `ci_aggregate.csv` to baseline.
- Keep the default run on the nightly perf suite (so we have one canonical artifact per commit).
- Add a smaller smoke job that runs the adaptor on golden synthetic traces for PRs touching runtime hot paths.

Output formats and fields
------------------------
1) folded (text): one-line folded stacks with weight for FlameGraph tools. Format: `module1;module2;… weight`
2) canonical JSONL: each line = canonical_event JSON with flat keys only (for compatibility with our trace explorer ingest). Required fields (string values except when noted):
   - event_id (string)
   - ts (ISO8601 string)
   - dur_ms (string)
   - request_id (string)
   - provenance (comma-separated sources)
